title: Full-screen collapse can get stuck when leave-full-screen never fires
reasoning: collapseMainWindowToChatPill on macOS full-screen waits only for the leave-full-screen event before hiding the main window and showing the chat pill. Unlike focusWindowForPermissionPrompt, which includes a timeout fallback for the same leave-full-screen transition, collapseMainWindowToChatPill has no timeout or error path. If Electron or macOS does not emit the event, the main window remains visible, the chat pill is not shown, and __windiePendingCollapseToChatPill stays true so future close attempts return immediately.
reproduction: On macOS, close the dashboard while it is full-screen and simulate or encounter a missed leave-full-screen event. The first close sets __windiePendingCollapseToChatPill and never calls finishCollapse; subsequent close attempts hit the pending guard and do nothing.
recommendation: Mirror the bounded wait pattern used by focusWindowForPermissionPrompt: install a timeout fallback, clear it when the event fires, and reset __windiePendingCollapseToChatPill in both success and fallback paths.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests cover macOS full-screen close/collapse transitions or missed leave-full-screen events.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a unit test for collapseMainWindowToChatPill that uses a fake mainWindow whose once('leave-full-screen') callback never fires, advances timers, and asserts hide/showChatWindow are called and the pending flag is cleared.
minimumFixScope: frontend/src/main/main_window_runtime.cjs collapseMainWindowToChatPill plus a focused timer-based unit test.
